section: Foundation of Vijayanagara - Harihara and Bukka, Vidyaranya; the Sangama dynasty
subsections: Sangama campaigns in Andhra (Bukka I, Devaraya II) - Kondavidu, Udayagiri, Rayalaseema forts, court poets

accepted.s: Which of the following places were captured by Bukka I during his campaigns in Andhra?
accepted.x: Bukka I captured Srisailam and Dupadu, the latter being near Markapur.
accepted.tq: Use the place-pair to distinguish Bukka I’s campaign from those of the later Sangama rulers.
accepted.sec: Sangama campaigns in Andhra (Bukka I, Devaraya II) - Kondavidu, Udayagiri, Rayalaseema forts, court poets  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Harihara II advanced towards the Krishna in alliance with which of the following?
accepted.x: Harihara II pushed towards the Krishna in alliance with the Reddis.
accepted.tq: Identify the allied power by separating Harihara II’s campaign from Devaraya I’s alliances.
accepted.sec: Sangama campaigns in Andhra (Bukka I, Devaraya II) - Kondavidu, Udayagiri, Rayalaseema forts, court poets  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Devaraya I:
1. He fought the Kandukuru Reddis and made them feudatories.
2. He allied with the Velamas and Kataya Vema.
3. He captured Srisailam and Dupadu near Markapur.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the capture of Srisailam and Dupadu is attributed to Bukka I.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong ruler–achievement pairing before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Sangama campaigns in Andhra (Bukka I, Devaraya II) - Kondavidu, Udayagiri, Rayalaseema forts, court poets  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Devaraya I’s capture of southern Kondaveedu, including Motupalli, is recorded in which inscription?
accepted.x: Devaraya I’s capture of southern Kondaveedu, including Motupalli, is recorded in the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam.
accepted.tq: Match the specific inscription with the ruler’s territorial achievement.
accepted.sec: Sangama campaigns in Andhra (Bukka I, Devaraya II) - Kondavidu, Udayagiri, Rayalaseema forts, court poets  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Harihara II — advance towards the Krishna with Reddi support
Devaraya I — southern Kondaveedu and Motupalli
Devaraya II — capture of Dupadu near Markapur
accepted.x: Dupadu near Markapur was captured by Bukka I, not Devaraya II. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Check the ruler associated with each campaign and identify the swapped achievement.
accepted.sec: Sangama campaigns in Andhra (Bukka I, Devaraya II) - Kondavidu, Udayagiri, Rayalaseema forts, court poets  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Devaraya II sent Mallappa Odayar to assist which place?
accepted.x: Devaraya II sent Mallappa Odayar to help Rajahmundry, as recorded in the Draksharama inscription of 1444.
accepted.tq: Use the person–place association to distinguish Devaraya II’s intervention in Andhra.
accepted.sec: Sangama campaigns in Andhra (Bukka I, Devaraya II) - Kondavidu, Udayagiri, Rayalaseema forts, court poets  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Draksharama inscription associated with Devaraya II’s assistance to Rajahmundry is dated to:
accepted.x: The Draksharama inscription referring to Mallappa Odayar’s assistance to Rajahmundry is dated 1444.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the inscription date from the foundation and terminal dates of the Sangama period.
accepted.sec: Sangama campaigns in Andhra (Bukka I, Devaraya II) - Kondavidu, Udayagiri, Rayalaseema forts, court poets  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who among the following was the author of Kridabhiramam and served as governor of Vinukonda under Devaraya II?
accepted.x: Vinukonda Vallabharaya wrote Kridabhiramam and was the governor of Vinukonda under Devaraya II.
accepted.tq: Link the author, work and office rather than confusing the poet with a military officer or ally.
accepted.sec: Sangama campaigns in Andhra (Bukka I, Devaraya II) - Kondavidu, Udayagiri, Rayalaseema forts, court poets  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
With reference to the newly reported copper plates connected with Devaraya I’s coronation, consider the following statements:
1. They belong to the early fifteenth century.
2. They are written in Sanskrit, Kannada and Nagari.
3. They grant Gudipalli village, which was renamed Devarayapura-Agrahara.
4. They contain a full Sangama genealogy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The copper plates relate to Devaraya I’s coronation, use Sanskrit, Kannada and Nagari, record the grant and renamed village, and contain a full Sangama genealogy.
accepted.tq: Test a cluster of inscriptional details by eliminating any statement that mismatches the record.

accepted.s: The copper plates associated with Devaraya I’s coronation record how many shares for the grant of Gudipalli village, renamed Devarayapura-Agrahara?
accepted.x: The grant of Gudipalli, renamed Devarayapura-Agrahara, is recorded as comprising 61 shares.
accepted.tq: Treat the precise numerical figure as a separate inscriptional fact rather than inferring it from the date or genealogy.

accepted.s: Which symbol appears on the seal of the copper plates connected with Devaraya I’s coronation?
accepted.x: The copper plates carry a Vamana seal, rather than the usual Varaha seal.
accepted.tq: Focus on the exceptional symbol and avoid reversing the unusual seal with the customary one.

accepted.s: The copper plates associated with Devaraya I’s coronation were unveiled in:
accepted.x: The copper plates were unveiled in Bengaluru.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the place of discovery or unveiling from the later capitals associated with the empire.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the inscriptions copied in the Nallamala Tiger Reserve:
1. They range from the second to the sixteenth century CE.
2. They include Vijayanagara records.
3. They were copied from the Seshachalam hills.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the inscriptions in question were copied in the Nallamala Tiger Reserve; the Seshachalam reference concerns a separate set of inscriptions.
accepted.tq: Keep geographically adjacent Andhra sites distinct when testing inscriptional evidence.

accepted.s: Which of the following places are specifically associated with the Vijayanagara Empire’s Andhra Pradesh connection?
accepted.x: Udayagiri, Kondaveedu, Penukonda and Chandragiri are identified as places linking the empire with Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure place-pair and select the complete geographical grouping.

accepted.s: Which ruler is identified as the first Vijayanagara ruler to attack Sri Lanka?
accepted.x: Harihara II is identified as the first Vijayanagara ruler to attack Sri Lanka.
accepted.tq: Separate the first external attack from the foreign-traveller association and Andhra campaigns.

accepted.s:
With reference to the dynastic and geographical features of the Vijayanagara Empire, consider the following statements:
1. Sangama and Aravidu are described as two dynasties of Andhra origin.
2. Penukonda and Chandragiri served as later capitals and are located in Andhra Pradesh.
3. All four Vijayanagara dynasties are described as Andhra in origin.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because only two of the four dynasties, Sangama and Aravidu, are described as Andhra in origin.
accepted.tq: Reject the extreme claim that extends a correct two-dynasty classification to all four dynasties.

accepted.s: Sixteenth-century inscriptions reported from Seshachalam are dated to which period of Vijayanagara history?
o: The late Aravidu or post-Vijayanagara period
The Tuluva or early Aravidu period
accepted.x: The inscriptions reported from Seshachalam are dated to the Tuluva or early Aravidu period.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between successive Vijayanagara dynasties by identifying the correct period pair.
